name: Krystal Biotech, Inc.
moat_justification: VYJUVEK's orphan exclusivity, 95% gross margin, entrenched reimbursement/prescriber base and the redosable HSV-1 platform give a real but narrow moat: one product, one small patient pool, only two years of positive ROIC history, and competition (ZEVASKYN) now entering DEB. A 6 sits on ROIC that has only just crossed above the cost of capital (10.2% FY2024, 17.6% FY2025) — the written reason it is not 7+ is that the franchise has not yet held high ROIC through a cycle and revenue is a single therapy.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 5.5%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

SHARES_FALLBACK: no diluted share count filed for 2017, 2018, 2019 — those history years use the basic / outstanding / dei count recorded in the shares_tag column; per-share history there is approximate

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 4.49 vs 3-yr median 2.36 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (6.7%) vs bull-case tier C (10.2%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Profitable single-product gene-therapy leader (VYJUVEK at a 95% gross margin, debt-free, $1.1B cash), moat 6/10 — does not clear 15% at $320.25 (weighted IRR 8.7%, weighted IV@15% $138.98); it would clear the 15% hurdle only below ~$139.
moat_for: First and only FDA-approved redosable gene therapy for DEB (VYJUVEK, approved 2023, from birth); orphan-drug exclusivity and patent estate around the HSV-1 platform
95% gross margin (Q2 2026) on lean in-house manufacturing — structural cost advantage
Entrenched access: 730+ U.S. reimbursement approvals, 640+ prescribers, >60% penetration of the diagnosed U.S. DEB pool
Redosable HSV-1 platform carries an FDA Platform Technology Designation; registrational programs in eye (KB803, KB801), lung (KB407, KB408) and skin (KB111) reuse the same delivery engine
Returns inflecting: ROIC proxy -22% (2023) -> +10.2% (2024) -> +17.6% (2025) with a 44.9% TTM operating margin; debt-free with ~$1.1B cash and investments (Q2 2026)
moat_against: Single product: VYJUVEK is effectively 100% of revenue; the DEB patient pool is small and U.S. penetration already exceeds 60% of the diagnosed pool
Growth decelerating: FY2025 revenue +33.9%, TTM +22.6%, Q2 2026 +24% — the U.S. launch wave is maturing
Competition arriving: Abeona's ZEVASKYN (approved 2025) targets recessive DEB wounds; other DEB programs in development
European pricing/reimbursement still being negotiated (Italy/Spain launches pending) — ex-U.S. realized pricing uncertain
Pipeline beyond VYJUVEK is unproven: KB803/KB801/KB407/KB408/KB707 carry binary clinical risk, and SBC runs ~12-14% of revenue
